owner_posts.post_text:
This Men’s Health Month, let’s make space for conversations that feel easier to start.

Health discussions, especially around fertility and reproductive health, are often delayed because they feel confusing, uncomfortable, or overwhelming.

But clarity, openness, and understanding can make a meaningful difference. When people feel informed instead of intimidated, they are more likely to seek answers early and take confident steps towards their health.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe empathy begins with making every health conversation feel simple, transparent, and easier to navigate.

Male fertility is often overlooked until the journey to parenthood takes longer than expected.

But fertility is not only about sperm count. Sperm quality, including movement and overall health, can also play an important role in conception.
Advanced techniques like Microfluidics help select healthier moving sperm during IVF treatment, supporting a more personalised approach to fertility care.
This Men's Health Month, let's encourage earlier conversations, timely evaluations, and greater awareness around male fertility health.

Some dreams take a little longer to come true.

They begin as quiet hopes, become whispered prayers, and one day turn into the most beautiful reality.
This Father’s Day, we’re celebrating every dad who held on to hope, believed through the waiting, and never gave up on his dream of a family.

In IVF, precision matters at every stage.

From the collection of eggs and sperm to embryo transfer, accurate identification and verification play an important role throughout the treatment journey.

RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology adds an additional layer of electronic witnessing by assigning unique identifiers to biological samples and tracking them through key stages of the IVF process. This helps strengthen traceability and supports laboratory protocols designed to minimise the possibility of mix-ups.
At Nova IVF Fertility, RFID-based witnessing is integrated into our IVF laboratory processes as part of our commitment to maintaining high standards of safety and care.

A diagnosis of azoospermia can feel overwhelming, especially when a semen analysis shows no sperm. For many men, it may seem like the end of the road to fatherhood.

However, in some cases, sperm may still be present within the testes and can sometimes be retrieved through specialised procedures such as TESA, TESE or Micro-TESE. These retrieved sperm may then be used in IVF/ICSI treatment, offering some couples an opportunity to pursue pregnancy using their own sperm and eggs.
This Men’s Health Month, let’s remember that the right diagnosis and expert evaluation can make all the difference.

Father's Day: AI Now Reading Sperm, Giving Hope of Fatherhood to Infertile Men
Dr. PGL Lalit Kumar, Head of Embryology and Scientific Director, Nova IVF Fertility

AI is revolutionizing sperm analysis in fertility clinics by offering more accurate and consistent assessments. While AI aids in identifying rare sperm cells and improving treatment outcomes, experts stress it should complement, not replace, clinical expertise. The adoption of AI in fertility care is increasing, enhancing the precision and efficiency of evaluations.

This Men’s Health Month, it’s important to remember that a man’s health extends beyond just himself.

Physical health, emotional well-being, lifestyle habits, and reproductive health can all influence not only his own future, but also the well-being of his partner and the family he hopes to build.
Small everyday choices, timely health check-ups, and greater awareness can make a meaningful difference over time. Prioritising health today is also an investment in healthier tomorrows for the generations ahead.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe conversations around fertility and reproductive health should include men equally because awareness and early action matter for everyone involved.

Sometimes, supporting your fertility doesn’t require long hours at the gym, just a few intentional moments through the day. Even short bursts of movement can begin to make a difference to how your body responds

Exercise snacking,” or quick intervals of activity, is linked to better hormone balance, improved circulation, and lower stress levels. When done consistently, these small efforts can support your body more effectively than a sedentary routine.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we guide you towards simple, sustainable habits that work with your lifestyle, helping you move forward, one step at a time.

Around 15–20 eggs begin developing in your ovaries each month.

But the body naturally selects just one dominant egg and asks the rest to stop growing.
This is a normal biological process, not a limitation.
In IVF, this process is supported differently, allowing multiple eggs to continue developing for better chances of conception.
At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe awareness of your body helps you make more informed fertility choices.

Sometimes what feels like falling behind is just the body and mind taking a different path than expected.

There are moments in the fertility journey when things feel uncertain, when progress feels slow, and when answers do not come easily.
But with the right guidance, clarity slowly replaces confusion and support makes all the difference.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we focus on bringing structure to that uncertainty through informed decisions, scientific analysis, personalised support and expert guidance.

Not Conceiving Naturally? Understanding IVF Solutions

Not being able to conceive naturally can feel stressful and confusing for many couples. However, with the right medical support, there are effective solutions available that can significantly improve your chances of pregnancy.

Infertility can happen due to various reasons such as ovulation disorders, hormonal imbalance, blocked fallopian tubes, low sperm count, or unexplained factors. Identifying the exact cause through proper diagnosis is the first and most important step toward the right treatment.

When natural methods are not successful, assisted reproductive techniques are recommended. Depending on the condition, doctors may suggest IUI, IVF, or ICSI. IVF involves fertilising the egg and sperm in a laboratory and transferring the embryo into the uterus, while ICSI is a specialised method used mainly in male infertility cases. These IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments are designed to overcome specific fertility challenges with higher precision.

Timely consultation and personalised care can improve success rates and reduce unnecessary delays. With advancements in medical science, many couples are now able to achieve parenthood through IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments tailored to their needs.

What Makes an IVF Clinic the Right Choice?

Choosing the right IVF clinic is one of the most important decisions in your fertility journey. The right center not only offers advanced treatments but also provides transparency, trust, and personalised care at every step.

A good IVF clinic focuses on accurate diagnosis before starting any treatment. Every couple is different, and understanding the root cause of infertility helps in creating a tailored plan rather than following a standard approach. This improves outcomes and avoids unnecessary procedures.

Experienced specialists and skilled embryologists play a key role in success. From monitoring ovulation to embryo transfer, every stage requires precision and expertise. Clinics that use advanced technology and maintain high lab standards ensure better chances of fertilisation and embryo development.

Clear communication is equally important. A reliable clinic explains every step, expected outcomes, and possible challenges in simple terms. This helps couples stay informed and confident throughout the process.

Emotional support is often overlooked but essential. Fertility treatment can be stressful, and a compassionate team can make the journey smoother and more comfortable.

Choosing a clinic that offers complete care under one roof, including IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments, ensures continuity and better coordination. With the right support, couples can move forward with clarity and hope using IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments.

When Should You Consult a Fertility Specialist?

Many couples try to conceive naturally for months or even years before seeking medical advice. However, certain signs may indicate that it is the right time to consult a fertility specialist for proper evaluation and guidance.

One of the most common signs is trying for pregnancy for a long time without success. If a couple has been trying to conceive for over a year without results, or for six months if the woman is above 35, it may be time to seek medical support. Early consultation can help identify underlying causes and avoid delays in treatment.

Irregular menstrual cycles are another important indicator. Conditions such as hormonal imbalance or polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS) can affect ovulation and reduce the chances of natural conception. A specialist can assess these issues and recommend appropriate care.

Male fertility factors are also an important part of fertility evaluation. Low sperm count, poor motility, or other sperm-related concerns can affect conception. Proper diagnosis and treatment planning can help couples move forward with suitable options such as IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments when required.

Early diagnosis and timely care can significantly improve outcomes with IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments.

Foods to Avoid During IVF Treatment

Nutrition plays an important role during fertility care. While there is no strict “IVF diet,” certain foods are better avoided to support better outcomes and overall health during treatment.

Highly processed foods such as packaged snacks, fried items, and fast food should be limited. These foods are often high in trans fats, refined sugar, and preservatives that may affect hormonal balance. Excess sugar intake can also impact insulin levels, which is especially important for women with PCOS.

It is advisable to reduce caffeine consumption from coffee, energy drinks, and certain soft drinks. High caffeine intake may affect implantation in some cases. Alcohol should also be avoided during fertility treatment, as it can interfere with hormonal regulation and egg quality.

Raw or undercooked foods, including unpasteurised dairy, raw eggs, or uncooked seafood, should be avoided to reduce the risk of infection.

 High-mercury fish such as shark or swordfish are also not recommended. Maintaining a balanced diet supports the body during IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments and helps create a healthier environment for conception.

Hydration, fresh home-cooked meals, fruits, vegetables, lean proteins, and whole grains are generally preferred during IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments to maintain energy and stability.

Separating Truth from Myths About IVF

IVF is one of the most effective fertility treatments today, yet many myths create confusion and unnecessary fear. Understanding the facts helps couples take timely and confident decisions.

A common myth is that IVF always guarantees pregnancy. The fact is that IVF improves the chances of conception, but success depends on factors such as age, egg quality, sperm health, and overall medical condition. 

Another misconception is that IVF is extremely painful. In reality, most procedures are well-managed with modern techniques and patient-focused care, making them comfortable and safe.

Many believe IVF is only meant for women with severe fertility problems. In truth, IVF is advised for multiple conditions, including male infertility, blocked fallopian tubes, endometriosis, repeated miscarriages, and unexplained infertility. 

There is also a belief that IVF always results in twins or triplets. With careful embryo selection and transfer, the risk of multiple pregnancy is controlled.

Some couples worry that lifestyle changes do not matter during treatment. In fact, healthy nutrition, stress management, and following medical advice play an important role in improving outcomes with IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments. Another myth is that children born through IVF are not healthy, which is incorrect scientific evidence shows they grow and develop normally.

A Clear Guide to Egg Retrieval in IVF

Egg retrieval is one of the most important steps in the IVF process. It is a carefully planned medical procedure where mature eggs are collected from the ovaries so they can be fertilised in a laboratory. Understanding this step helps reduce fear and builds confidence before starting treatment.

Before egg retrieval, the ovaries are stimulated using fertility medications to help multiple eggs mature at the same time. During this phase, ultrasound scans and blood tests are done regularly to monitor follicle growth and hormone levels. Once the eggs (follicles) are ready, ovum pick-up (OPU) is timed very precisely after the trigger injection.
The procedure  is done under anesthesia Using ultrasound guidance, a thin needle is passed through the vaginal wall to gently collect the eggs from the ovaries. The procedure usually takes 15–20 minutes, and most patients can go home the same day after a short rest period.

The retrieved eggs are then assessed in the lab and used for fertilisation as part of IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments, depending on the individual treatment plan. Mild bloating or discomfort after the procedure is common and usually settles within a day or two.

Egg retrieval is safe, controlled, and done with precision to maximise success in IVF/ICSI Treatments.

Understanding Fertility Challenges with Medical Clarity

Fertility problems can affect both men and women, and in many cases, the cause is a combination of factors from both partners. Understanding these issues early helps couples take the right steps toward timely and effective treatment.

In women, common fertility problems include ovulation disorders, hormonal imbalance, polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), endometriosis, blocked fallopian tubes, and age-related decline in egg quality. Irregular periods, difficulty conceiving, or repeated miscarriages may indicate an underlying concern that needs proper evaluation.

Male fertility problems are equally common and often misunderstood. These may include low sperm count, poor sperm motility, abnormal sperm shape, hormonal issues, or blockages affecting sperm delivery. Lifestyle factors such as stress, smoking, obesity, and medical conditions can also impact male fertility.

Accurate diagnosis is the foundation of successful treatment. Blood tests, ultrasound scans, semen analysis, and other investigations help identify the root cause. Based on findings, doctors may recommend lifestyle changes, medications, or assisted reproductive options such as IVF, IUI, ICSI Treatments to improve the chances of conception.

featured_reviews.review_text: I had an exceptional experience with Dr. Anuja, who is truly a compassionate and highly skilled IVF specialist. featured_reviews.name: Abhishek Bawankar
featured_reviews.review_text:
I cannot describe in words how valuable our association is with Dr. Anuja. It isn't unknown to the world that having a kid is one of the most beautiful things that can ever happen to a couple. I will forever be thankful to Dr. Anuja for being a candid, honest and empathetic doctor.

She lends the perfect ear and doesn't go for unnecessary treatments. After struggling for years and consulting all big guns in the gynec world there were no results. No one told us the root cause of the problem. Dr. Anuja outlined the step by step plan for diagnosis and possible mitigation (treatment). Dr. Anjua has been through with us in the entire journey from consultation to conceiving & I am very thankful to her for bringing a miracle to our life.

I would definitely recommend her as an infertility specialist to other couples for the stress free process and best results.
